words.context: A greeting, not a question. “Grand, yourself?” closes it. “What’s the story?” does the same job.
The standard warm version, often compressed to “thanks a mil.” “Cheers” works fine too.
Said leaving a shop with no luck implied. “See you now” works, and so does a rapid string of byes.
Works for apologising and for getting past. Also means “what did you say?” and opens most requests.
Bar service runs on eye contact and patience. There’s no line at the bar but there is an order, and it’s tracked.
Asking for “the check” marks you immediately.
Often added for groups of six or more and stated on the menu. Check before you add anything on top.
The transit card for bus, Luas, and DART. Contactless bank cards do not work on Dublin buses.
Casual and very Dublin. Signs say “Toilets,” with “Leithreas” printed underneath.

words.groupNote: Irish, said feer and mnaw. On plenty of pub doors with no English at all, and genuinely easy to get wrong.

words.context: Also “the hole in the wall.” Ireland uses the euro, unlike Northern Ireland an hour up the road.
Contactless everywhere. Say it as you hold the card up.
Still worth carrying for older pubs and taxis, though card works nearly everywhere now.
Charged since 2002 — Ireland was the first country in the world to do it.
Fun, atmosphere, company, and news all at once. “What’s the craic?” is a greeting. Grim when marketed, real when not.
Fine, acceptable, no problem. Also what someone says when things are emphatically not fine. Tone is everything.
“The centre” — what city-center buses show as their destination. The single most useful piece of Irish for a visitor.
Excellent. Not dangerous, and not sarcastic.
That man, whose name I’m not supplying. “Yer one” for a woman. Fully functional as identification.
Mock insults traded between friends as a sign of affection. Being left out of it is the part to worry about.
The police. Plural “Gardaí,” said GAR-dee. Nobody here says “the police.”
House or apartment. “A free gaff” means the parents are away, which is the phrase’s main use.
